title: No More 4 AM Meows! These Smart Cat Feeders Are Game-Changers
summary:
Picture this: it's 4 AM, and your cat is yowling for food like a tiny, furry alarm clock. Sound familiar? Well, technology has a purr-fect solution! Automatic cat feeders are here to save your sleep and keep your kitty happy.

These aren't your grandma's gravity bowls. Today's feeders connect to Wi-Fi and an app on your phone. You can schedule meals, give snacks from anywhere, and even watch your cat eat through a built-in camera. Some models, like the Petkit YumShare Dual-Hopper 2 ($170), use AI to see how much food is left and stop dispensing so your cat doesn't turn into a chunky fluffball.

But the real star? The Petlibro Polar Smart Wet Feeder ($170). It's basically a mini-fridge for wet food! It keeps meals cool and fresh, then slides open a lid at mealtime. No more stinky, dried-out leftovers. The bowls are wide and shallow to protect your cat's sensitive whiskers, too.

WIRED tested 11 feeders and found options for every budget. The Petlibro Granary Camera Feeder ($100) has a sharp camera and easy app. For a simpler pick, the Petlibro Air Feeder ($60) is sleek and reliable. Even a dual-bowl model from Oneisall ($50) works great if you don't mind a basic app.

So, whether you have a greedy gobbler or a picky nibbler, there's a smart feeder out there. Your cat might still be bossy, but at least you can sleep in!
why_it_matters: If you have a pet, this technology can help you take better care of it, just like a smartwatch helps you stay healthy—and it might stop a lot of early-morning wake-up calls!

background_read: Petkit is a Chinese brand known for smart pet products, and Petlibro is another popular maker of automated feeders.
Automatic feeders first became available years ago as simple gravity-driven bowls, but now they include cameras, apps, and even AI.
WIRED is a magazine and website that tests all kinds of tech gadgets to help people decide what to buy.
Article_Structure: WHO: Cat owners who want to stop early-morning meowing and several smart feeder companies.
WHAT: New automatic cat feeders with Wi-Fi, cameras, AI, and even built-in fridges to keep food fresh.
WHERE: These devices are used in homes anywhere, controlled through phone apps.
WHY: So cats can be fed on a schedule or remotely, and owners can sleep better while keeping their cats from overeating.

perspectives.description: Owners love the convenience and peace of mind, knowing their cat is fed even when they are away or asleep.
Some experts worry that too much technology might replace human interaction with pets, which is important for bonding.
For people on a tight budget, the cheapest models work well enough, so you don't need to spend a lot to solve the yowling problem.
